cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: keeping on because you still hope
cells.place: in the shared meaning of the people around you
cells.ask: offer this steady holding to one thing you're already part of — the group, the tradition, the practice that keeps getting passed on — and let what you've carried long enough come through as light rather than effort.
cells.core:
You keep going, and the going has held. Not the loudest voice in the room and not a passenger — you stayed with what mattered long enough that it's still standing. What you've carried this far arrives as something others can stand on, which is why it holds.

The hope that started it is still in the work. Nothing about that has worn out.
cells.sheetLine: You keep going, and the keeping has held.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: pushing the hope harder than the ground can take it
cells.place: in the shared meaning of the people around you
cells.ask: take one thing you're carrying ahead of time and hold it without declaring where it must land — let the knowing settle before you speak, and the way you stay with it will read as light rather than strain.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead there's a version where the thing finally holds without effort, and you're living in that version — so every conversation becomes proof, every group becomes the test, every tradition becomes something you're pressing forward before its time. The pushing is costing you the very ground pushing was for.

The hope is real. The bracing is not the same as the hope.
cells.sheetLine: You're pressing for forward proof of what hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: no longer carrying what you still believe in
cells.place: in the shared meaning of the people around you
cells.ask: tend one small thing in that shared life — a ritual, a phrase, a practice — with care that doesn't exhaust you, and let the growing happen without forcing it; the aliveness of the ground will come back as light when you stop carrying your own staying-power alone.
cells.core:
You believe in something and you've stopped standing in it. Somewhere back there, the shared thing stopped feeling worth the staying, and you stepped out of the room you were meant to keep warm. The belief hasn't gone anywhere. The standing has.

The people around you are still passing something on. You just aren't one of the hands anymore.
cells.sheetLine: You still believe it. You stopped standing in it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: holding steady without claiming the steadying
cells.place: in the shared meaning of the people around you
cells.ask: admit one place where you're the one holding it together — the tradition, the tone, the thing that only keeps going because you keep it going — and let that steady holding contain what it's been containing without you calling it just how things are.
cells.core:
You're the one keeping this going — the shared thing only stands because you've quietly held it — and you talk about it as if it ran on its own. The holding is running. The name on it isn't.

The strength is yours. You just haven't said so.
cells.sheetLine: You're the reason it holds. You haven't said so.
